scope: Corollary 6.6 (Finite marked histories) of the manuscript “The Boltzmann–Grad limit for stable radial potentials on regular kinetic intervals” (preprints/The-Boltzmann-Grad-limit-for-stable-radial-potentials-on-regular-kinetic-intervals-September-23-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 364 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 dce9fe5976f17b89), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 54. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Fix the layer count and an integer p∗. Sum the absolute integrals of the original prescribed histories with at most p∗ labels, integrating all top phase points, and suppose their independent source norms in (6.9) are uniformly bounded. The contribution with at least one unprescribed contact, an incomplete isolated scattering at a required cut, an interfering birth, or an endpoint-polymer defect tends to zero as ε ↓ 0. This statement includes p = h0 and contacts between distinct top roots. The bounds are uniform over the observation times and shortened endpoint cells in the fixed interval. If instead a source has norm tending to zero, its finite-history integral tends to zero by the same uniform finite-size majorant.
